criteria.quote: Aerodactyl ruled the sky, but ground makes it weak.
criteria.revision: Replace the opening with: "Aerodactyl was imagined as the king of ancient skies—but one Pokédex entry describes its walk as weak and slow." This keeps the contrast while avoiding the unsupported claim that touching ground makes Aerodactyl itself weak.

criteria.quote: Ancient Pokédex entries picture it ruling skies above the dinosaur age.
criteria.revision: Replace this general summary with a concrete detail: "Its sawlike fangs could shred even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon—and it was still described as having a weak, slow walk on the ground."

criteria.quote: How can a sky king become so awkward on the ground?
criteria.revision: Reframe the open loop around the documented contradiction: "What does the Pokédex actually say happens when this supposed sky king touches ground?" The research gives no explanation for why its walk is weak and slow, so the script should not imply one.

criteria.quote: It flew through ancient skies as if they belonged to it.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated sky-dominance beat with a new escalation: "But this ancient predator was not merely intimidating—its sawlike fangs could shred even Steel-type skin." Then reveal the weak, slow walk as the contrast.

criteria.quote: Then it touches ground, and its walk turns weak and slow.
criteria.revision: Delay the exact reveal until this scene and make the earlier hook less explicit: open with "Aerodactyl was imagined as king of the skies. Then one entry describes what happens on land." This preserves the documented twist without announcing it twice before the reveal.

criteria.quote: "KING OF ANCIENT SKIES" / "THE SKY WAS ITS OWN" / "THE LANDING CHANGES EVERYTHING" / "Ferocious or not, its ground walk stays weak and slow."
criteria.revision: Cut or combine the two sky scenes, then use the freed scene for a distinct fact: "Its fangs can shred the skin of Steel-type Pokémon." The current middle repeatedly restates sky dominance and grounded weakness.

criteria.quote: Aerodactyl owns the open skies, yet its Pokédex entry gives it a weak, slow walk on land.
criteria.revision: End with the sharper evidence-based contrast: "The Pokédex imagines Aerodactyl as king of the skies, but says its walk is weak and slow—and its fangs can still shred even Steel-type skin."

Replace it with a genuine interpretive split: "Which matters more: being imagined as king of the skies, or having a weak and slow walk on land?" Both sides are directly grounded in the Pokédex entries.
